district.name: Bengaluru Urban
district.description: The dynamic capital city and tech hub of India, featuring Tudor-style Bangalore Palace, 240-acre Lalbagh Botanical Garden, Tipu's Summer Palace, Bannerghatta Biological Safari, and the 890 CE Begur inscription.
district.descriptionKannada: ಭಾರತದ ಸಿಲಿಕಾನ್ ಸಿಟಿ ಮತ್ತು ರಾಜಧಾನಿ, ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ಅರಮನೆ, ಲಾಲ್‌ಬಾಗ್ ಸಸ್ಯತೋಟ, ಟಿಪ್ಪು ಸುಲ್ತಾನ್ ಬೇಸಿಗೆ ಅರಮನೆ, ಬನ್ನೇರುಘಟ್ಟ ಜೈವಿಕ ಉದ್ಯಾನ ಮತ್ತು ೮೯೦ರ ಬೇಗೂರು ಶಾಸನವನ್ನು ಒಳಗೊಂಡಿದೆ.

destinations.name: Bangalore Palace
destinations.description: A magnificent Tudor-style royal palace inspired by Windsor Castle, built by Maharaja Chamarajendra Wadiyar X in 1887. Features fortified towers, wood carvings, floral motifs, stained glass, and historic royal oil paintings by Raja Ravi Varma.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Purchased in 1873 from Rev. J. Garrett and reconstructed as the city royal residence of the Wodeyar dynasty.
destinations.culturalImportance: Premier architectural icon of Bengaluru, hosting royal gatherings, state functions, and world-class musical performances.

photos.caption: Bangalore Palace
photos.source: Mysuru Royal Family Trust & Karnataka Tourism

destinations.nearestBusStation: Cantonment / Shivaji Nagar Bus Stand (2 km)
destinations.nearestRailwayStation: Bangalore Cantonment (2 km) or KSR Bengaluru (4 km)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Central city road, easily accessible by Metro, cab, or bus
destinations.safetyInstructions: Audio guides available in English and Kannada. Photography requires additional token.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Entry ticket required at palace counter
destinations.tourismInformationSource: Mysuru Royal Family Trust & Karnataka Tourism

destinations.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden & Glass House
destinations.description: A 240-acre botanical paradise home to India's largest collection of tropical plants, centenarian trees, the historic 1889 Glass House modeled on London's Crystal Palace, and the 3,000-million-year-old Peninsular Gneiss National Geological Monument.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Commissioned in 1760 by Hyder Ali and expanded by Tipu Sultan who imported exotic plants from Persia, Kabul, and France.
destinations.culturalImportance: Heartbeat of Bengaluru's 'Garden City' identity; host of the famous Republic Day and Independence Day biannual flower shows.

photos.caption: Lalbagh Botanical Garden & Glass House
photos.source: Department of Horticulture, Government of Karnataka

destinations.bestSeason: Year-round (Flower shows in January and August)
destinations.nearestBusStation: Lalbagh Main Gate Bus Stop (0.1 km)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Directly connected via Namma Metro Green Line (Lalbagh Station)
destinations.safetyInstructions: Do not pluck flowers or disturb nesting birds. Electric buggies available for seniors.
destinations.tourismInformationSource: Department of Horticulture, Government of Karnataka

destinations.name: Begur Nageshwara Temple Complex (Earliest 'Bengaluru' Inscription)
destinations.description: A magnificent 9th-century Western Ganga and Chola five-shrine (Panchalingeshwara) temple complex. Houses the historic Begur Hero Stone inscription of 890 CE, containing the earliest epigraphical record of the name 'Bengaluru' (Bengaluru Yuddha).
destinations.historicalSignificance: Epigraphical birthplace of the city's name; records the martyrdom of commander Nagattara's son Buttannashetty in the battle of Bengaluru in 890 CE.
destinations.culturalImportance: Supreme historical landmark establishing Bengaluru's antiquity extending over 1,130 years before Kempe Gowda.

photos.caption: Begur Nageshwara Temple Complex (Earliest 'Bengaluru' Inscription)
photos.source: Archaeological Survey of India & Epigraphia Carnatica

destinations.nearestRailwayStation: Carmelaram Railway Station (9 km) or KSR Bengaluru (16 km)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Paved city road connecting Hosur Road / Electronic City to Begur
destinations.safetyInstructions: Remove footwear before entering the temple compound. Respect the ancient hero stone inscriptions.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Protected by Archaeological Survey of India
destinations.tourismInformationSource: Archaeological Survey of India & Epigraphia Carnatica

destinations.name: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace & Bangalore Fort
destinations.nameKannada: ಟಿಪ್ಪು ಸುಲ್ತಾನರ ಬೇಸಿಗೆ ಅರಮನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ಕೋಟೆ
destinations.description: An exquisite two-storey Indo-Islamic summer palace constructed entirely in pure teakwood, completed in 1791 by Tipu Sultan. Features elaborately fluted teak pillars, floral corbels, and an ASI museum, paired with the surviving 1537 Kempe Gowda stone Delhi Gate and bastions of Bangalore Fort.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Tipu Sultan used it as his summer residence and called it 'Rashk-e-Jannat' (Envy of Heaven); Lord Cornwallis breached Bangalore Fort here during the 1791 Third Anglo-Mysore War.
destinations.culturalImportance: A treasured architectural testament to pre-colonial wooden engineering and Kempe Gowda's municipal origins in central Bengaluru.

photos.caption: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace & Bangalore Fort

destinations.distanceFromNearestTown: Located at KR Market, central Bengaluru
destinations.nearestBusStation: KR Market / Victoria Hospital Bus Stop (0.2 km)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Central city road; Metro Green Line (KR Market station 300m)
destinations.safetyInstructions: Remove footwear inside palace museum rooms. Photography permitted without flash.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Protected by Archaeological Survey of India

destinations.name: Nrityagram Classical Dance Village & Hesaraghatta Lake
destinations.nameKannada: ನೃತ್ಯಗ್ರಾಮ ಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೀಯ ನೃತ್ಯ ಗ್ರಾಮ ಮತ್ತು ಹೆಸರಘಟ್ಟ ಕೆರೆ
destinations.description: India's first modern classical dance gurukul, founded in 1990 by Odissi prima ballerina Protima Gauri. Designed by celebrated eco-architect Gerard da Cunha with mud, thatch, and natural granite, nestled beside ancient banyan trees and Hesaraghatta lake grasslands.
destinations.historicalSignificance: A modern cultural milestone reviving the ancient Guru-Shishya parampara; home to internationally acclaimed touring Odissi dancers.
destinations.culturalImportance: Unique retreat blending traditional arts, yoga, mud architecture, organic farming, and avian wetlands.

photos.caption: Nrityagram Classical Dance Village & Hesaraghatta Lake

destinations.bestSeason: October to March (Spring dance festival Vasantahabba)
destinations.roadAccessibility: Paved rural road via Jalahalli and Hesaraghatta
destinations.safetyInstructions: Maintain silence near dance practice halls. Advance email/booking recommended.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Nrityagram Trust managed; visitor entry fee applies

destinations.name: Bannerghatta Biological Park & Butterfly Dome
destinations.nameKannada: ಬನ್ನೇರುಘಟ್ಟ ಜೈವಿಕ ಉದ್ಯಾನವನ ಮತ್ತು ಚಿಟ್ಟೆ ಪಾರ್ಕ್
destinations.description: A 260-sq-km ecological sanctuary just south of Bengaluru, housing India's first butterfly conservatory with a 10,000-sq-ft polycarbonate dome, grand tiger, lion, bear, and herbivore safaris, and an elephant sanctuary in natural scrub forests.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Established in 1971; recognized as a crucial elephant migratory corridor linking the Eastern and Western Ghats.
destinations.culturalImportance: Premier wildlife education destination in Karnataka, pioneering large-carnivore rescue and rehabilitation.

photos.caption: Bannerghatta Biological Park & Butterfly Dome
photos.source: Zoo Authority of Karnataka & Forest Dept

destinations.roadAccessibility: Direct BMTC air-conditioned buses and 4-lane Bannerghatta Road
destinations.trekkingDifficulty: Easy (safari bus and paved zoo walks)
destinations.safetyInstructions: Stay inside safari vehicles. Never feed zoo animals. Buggies available for seniors.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Zoo Authority of Karnataka online/counter tickets
destinations.tourismInformationSource: Zoo Authority of Karnataka & Forest Dept
